checks.name: one leased account, ordinary native PKCE and hosted cookie profiles select the same real workspace
at least five paired fresh-process launches reach the same usable seeded chat
two leased browser identities remain private in main and the real account/workspace menu switches back to the retained owner
real sandboxed frame has no IPC/Node or parent access, and its API request never reaches the main bearer transport
actual main HTTP transport outage preserves the loaded conversation and unsent draft; online notification recovers
native notification click event follows the real preload bridge to the requested task/thread
native dialog result traverses real IPC and main validates the selected Git repository and cancellation
fresh-process offline launch serves installed assets and a meaningful local offline screen, then recovers without a reload

measurement.clock: Node performance.now, immediately before Electron launch to visible seeded message and enabled composer accepting a draft
measurement.process: same compiled shell/backend, bundled vs preserved hosted loading path; fresh Electron process for every sample, existing authenticated profile, same account/workspace
measurement.cache: normal profile/OS caches; no OS cache purge, artificial network delay or renderer response substitution
measurement.daemon: after every sample, cancel installers, close Electron and prove that exact profile daemon exited before launching the next process; drain time is outside readiness timing
measurement.preparation: one owned installed-app profile; both loading modes must reach a real registered online local device before the unchanged cold samples

source.process: primary API shared by lifecycle bundled, hosted and Chromium

queryCounts.scope: all actual pg.Client.query calls and PostgreSQL protocol bytes in the primary API process; no sampling
exclusions: test-account lease/session tracking and fixture SQL in the separate harness process
PostgreSQL connection handshake and TCP/TLS overhead
queryCounts.background: all concurrent primary API background traffic is included; no guessed subtraction or per-request attribution
queryCounts.boundary: query calls started and protocol bytes transferred by each checkpoint; in-flight response bytes can cross a checkpoint

login.authentication: normal email sign-in and get-session through the original leased-account helper; freshly saved private storageState
login.native: the same email authentication, then real PKCE with the authenticated browser session and initial renderer/workspace selection
login.web: the same email authentication, then a new actual Chromium context and the same workspace selection
login.sessionCache: normal signed-cookie cache, no manual flush; cache hits are not measured
login.comparisonBasis: common ordinary authentication and same usable workspace; native includes its additional PKCE transport
login.order: short Web context closes first; native and hosted retain the final ordinary login through the unchanged lifecycle checks
login.protocolPhases: native handoff overlaps automatic renderer navigation; these concurrent queries are not falsely separated
login.accountAndWorkspace: same leased owner and existing seeded fixture

startup.samples: first pair only from the unchanged five-pair lifecycle sequence
startup.clients: bundled Electron and the preserved hosted Web renderer in the same compiled Electron shell
startup.sessionCache: same retained authenticated app profile/workspace; normal profile and OS caches, no purge
startup.backend: same primary API and fixed source; server is already warm

boundary.assignment: requests belong to the half-open window [startedAt, finishedAt) containing their api_request_started timestamp
boundary.counts: physical HTTP RPC requests, not logical batch items or SQL calls; all primary API requests are included, without user attribution
boundary.overlap: completedInWindow includes carried-in requests; crossesStart/crossesEnd are confirmed by paired receipts and are not additive
boundary.statusCounts: observed completions of requests intersecting the window, including completions after its end
boundary.unknown: completionNotObserved means no completion in this one log snapshot, not proof the request is still running; without a start its window remains unknown
boundary.segments: closed measurement phases partition a completed window; starts belong to one phase, while completions and crossings remain separate non-additive observations

boundary.assignment: requests belong to the half-open window [startedAt, finishedAt) containing their api_request_started timestamp
boundary.counts: logical action invocations: each ordinary HTTP RPC once, each read-batch item once; batch envelopes excluded; not SQL calls
boundary.overlap: completedInWindow includes carried-in requests; crossesStart/crossesEnd are confirmed by paired receipts and are not additive
boundary.statusCounts: logical action result statuses; they are not additional HTTP responses
boundary.unknown: completionNotObserved means no completion in this one log snapshot, not proof the request is still running; without a start its window remains unknown
boundary.segments: closed measurement phases partition a completed window; starts belong to one phase, while completions and crossings remain separate non-additive observations
boundary.batchEvidence: each item is paired and bound to its physical request; the parent completion count detects missing entire item pairs

queryDiagnostics.boundary: SQL calls belong to (before.queryCalls, after.queryCalls]; completion times never choose a SQL window. IDs show ALS origin, including inherited background work; a captured null action is never backfilled. Structure equality proves neither equal parameters nor redundant work.
